headline: Secondary textbook printing lags as new academic year approaches; 4 new books await approval
summary: With just two months left until the new academic year, concerns rise over whether all students will receive their textbooks on time due to significant delays in secondary-level printing. Only 3% of Class 9-10 books have been supplied so far.
details: Nearly 31 crore textbooks for pre-primary to Class 9-10 are being printed for the upcoming academic year. While primary level printing is progressing well, significant delays are noted in the secondary level. This raises concerns about timely delivery for all students.
Currently, only about 3% of Class 9-10 textbooks have been supplied. Furthermore, printing orders for four new books, two each for Class 4 and Class 6, have not yet been issued.

Officials from the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) aim to complete printing by November 30 and ensure all students receive their textbooks by January. They express confidence in meeting the deadline.

Historically, ensuring all students receive textbooks on time has been a recurring challenge since the government began providing free books in 2010. Last academic year, it took over a month after the start to supply 100% of textbooks.

Out of the total 31 crore books, over 22 crore are for the secondary level and approximately 8.21 crore for the primary level. The estimated cost for printing these textbooks is around BDT 1,879 crore.
As of October 20, over 86% of primary level books were printed, with 74% supplied. For secondary level, about 50% of the first phase tender books were printed by October 21, and 40% supplied.

The four new books for Class 4 are 'Bangladesh's Culture' and 'Sports', while for Class 6 they are 'My Technical Education' and 'Joyful Education'. Approval for these books is expected from the National Curriculum Coordination Committee (NCCC) meeting on October 25.

headline_marked: [[3,000 tourists stranded in Sajek]] after clashes and reported gunfight; 7 security personnel injured
headline: 3,000 tourists stranded in Sajek after clashes and reported gunfight; 7 security personnel injured
summary: Around 3,000 tourists were safely evacuated from Sajek to Khagrachhari following a road blockade, clashes between protesters and law enforcers, and an alleged gunfight. Seven security personnel were injured in the incidents.
details: Around 3,000 tourists were stranded on the road from Sajek in Rangamati yesterday after clashes between blockade supporters and law enforcers, followed by a reported gunfight between the UPDF and security forces. They were later escorted to Khagrachhari.

The army and police jointly conducted the evacuation operation. Five army personnel and two police members sustained injuries during the clashes, though no tourists were harmed, according to Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib.

The blockade was enforced by the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association. Their demands include the removal of an armed group allegedly affiliated with the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS).

Protesters placed logs across the road, intercepting a column of about 450 tourist vehicles near Gangaram Bazar, 25km from Sajek Valley. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) stated that dialogue attempts failed.

ISPR claimed that around 10:45 am, protesters, allegedly instigated by United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) members, began throwing brick chunks and stones at law enforcers and tourists. Law enforcers used truncheons to disperse them.

ISPR further reported that armed UPDF members fired 30-40 shots at law enforcers and tourists around 11:00 am, prompting army personnel to return fire in self-defence. The armed men then fled, and tourists were evacuated.

The ISPR alleged that the blockade and violence were planned, with UPDF members intimidating locals into joining and using them as human shields. They also claimed UPDF members moved into tourist areas due to ongoing security operations.

However, UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma described reports of a gunfight as "completely false and fabricated." He alleged security personnel fired shots to break up a peaceful blockade and condemned what he called attacks and intimidation.

Babudhan Chakma, convener of the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee, also disputed the security forces' account. He claimed law enforcers first used truncheons and then fired on protesters, alleging over 57 civilian injuries and prevention of hospital access.

Tourist Sanjida Akter expressed her fear and anxiety during the blockade but relief upon reaching Khagrachhari safely. The district administration had suspended tourist travel and asked visitors to leave by Thursday afternoon after the indefinite blockade was announced.
